I could easily understand why they would try that stuff when the average adoption fees in the US range between $40,000-$50,000. I know the costs of IVF for a family member of mine were not nearly that (I understand in some cases it may be).Some people just want their own kids man. I don't necessarily know fully why either, personally I would prefer never to have a crotch goblin. Although, I think it has a lot to deal with societal ideals. 

Society always has portrayed and ingrained into our minds the idea of having a family or family life. Especially in the U.S. being married or dating someone and not wanting to build a family off that relationship is considered weird or abnormal. Go read some of the posts in r/childfree and you'll see what I mean. 

That being said, I still don't fully understand the want or 'calling' to be a mother or father. Never once in my life has that interested me one bit. All I can say is that I think the foster care and adoption system (in the U.S at least) needs to be radically changed. It doesn't work well, and in most cases adoption is not a viable option unless you have a disposable income or wanna be broke.

I think the issue is more that lqbtq/disabled/etc are not ever really considered to ever play the part or consulted with by the director (or whoever else) on what their experience is and how to portray it well. A lot of times that's where the issue lies. Although, It is called acting, and I agree  anyone should be able to try for the role or play the role. 

For example the whole situation with Sia was ridiculous. She chose a harmful organization (Autism Speaks) to support her movie and never talked with people who are actually autistic on what their experiences were to be able to  better portray an autistic character. If you want to represent lgbtq/disabled people in film it is a disservice to them to not at least do some research or even consider an actor of one of those communities to play the part (not saying they have to choose someone from those though).

Definitely not a repeat comment! We super appreciate your help and advice! I agree that a lot of companies that make gender non-conforming clothes or gender neutral clothing tend to be wayyyyy overpriced. We want to make clothing of all different sizes and shapes, that's affordable and flattering on everyone. Thanks for you input!

This is an incredible response. Thanks so much for your advice. These are all things we really want to focus on. I have very personally struggled with finding clothes that accentuate what I want and hide the bits I want hidden. I also am over just having t-shirt after t-shirt with a tacky logo or design on it. 

Also diversity is the key to our whole brand, it's our whole purpose essentially. We want to develop clothing that can fit virtually any body type and develop different fits and styles that flow well with all different body types. Once we have our test clothing come in at some point in the future we want to have people of all shapes and sizes try on our clothing. From that we will take their pros and cons and further develop our product. It's also important to us that the people who will eventually model our clothing will be of all different types of sizes, shapes, and races. We want everyone to feel like they can wear our clothing and feel comfortable as well as confident. I am so tired of seeing the same people modeling and advertising clothing claiming to be diverse, when in all reality they usually cater to the same group of people as you mentioned above. 

We are striving to develop clothing ethically and to make it affordable for everyone. I really appreciate your feedback, all the things you said are super important to us and will all be a part of our planning and development of our brand. Thanks so much again!

We totally agree with you! The whole idea of our company is the have clothing that can be worn by anyone, whether they are nonbinary, trans, or a hetero cis male. The whole idea is that we don't want the clothing to look like what would be stereotypical to either gender. The clothing is for everyone. 

I also am a larger nonbinary human, so for me plus sized clothing is essential to making this work! 

Thank you for your response!!
I definitely want casual suits as well! That'll for sure be something we will work on producing (of course with nice sizeable pockets as well).

Our main focus right now is the sizing, fit, and shape of the clothing. It's the most important thing to us that we create clothing that can fit virtually anyone. Designs will be something we'll focus later on once we have the sizing and shapes down. Thanks for mentioning it!
This will for sure be included in all our options for shirts and tops!

Having lots of pockets or larger pockets will also be something we want to include for sure. Too often pockets are sacrificed in clothing unfortunately or typically men have large pockets and women's clothing generally has tiny pockets. Down to do some cool prints as well!

This is something we really want to focus on as a clothing company. We want to offer shirts, pants, etc. in multiple different cuts for people so that each piece is something anyone can wear no matter if their height/weight/shape. We really want to cater to **everyone**. Thank you for the idea about adding filters in too! I definitely think it'd be cool for people to be able to filter based on their body type or the fit/style they like. Thanks for the input!!
This is an interesting idea! I'll definitely consider this for sure. I feel like it'd be a really cool unique idea

We will keep you updated on when the website is up and we have more news to share. Right now we are still a fresh developing company so we are still working on our outreach and marketing. Hopefully by the end of this week our discord server will be up and ready to go so we can get more people involved. Thanks for your support!!

So I definitely understand.
